target_customer: Capital markets, energy, aerospace and robotics teams needing fast time-series ingestion and queries
problem: Existing time-series databases were too slow or costly for high-throughput real-time workloads such as trading data.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) database with paid Enterprise and hosted cloud

founders.name: Nicolas Hourcard
founders.background_notes: CEO per YC page and TechCrunch; background not in opened sources.

founders.name: Vlad Ilyushchenko
founders.background_notes: YC page: software engineer in electronic trading; began the project as a side project (the original name was nfsdb per a database directory).

founders.name: Tancrede Collard
founders.background_notes: YC page: ran algorithmic trading desks at banks and cryptocurrency firms; listed as former founder.

competitors.name: InfluxDB
competitors.traction_then: established market leader per RedMonk profile

competitors.name: TimescaleDB
competitors.traction_then: a TimescaleDB co-founder questioned QuestDB benchmark claims on the Launch HN thread

competitors.name: kdb+
competitors.what: Proprietary columnar database used in financial time-series

competitors.name: ClickHouse
competitors.what: Columnar OLAP database used for analytics

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a new database engine in Java and zero-GC code with SIMD speed claims was demanding; the founder built it over years before the company.

defensibility.rationale: Open source gives adoption but also lets rivals copy; database migration costs create stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy or buy QuestDB; it stayed independent and now cites 7 of 20 largest investment banks.

market_need_then: TechCrunch Nov 2021 reported 900+ developers in Slack and 70+ contributors, and customers wanted a hosted version, indicating developer and enterprise demand; the 2020 launch had a trading data use case.

branding.domain_note: questdb.io was used earlier and questdb.com is now primary.
branding.brand_signature: Tiered swag program (stickers, pen, T-shirt) for open source contributors

rebrands.why: Not stated; date and former name from a database directory, not a primary source.

branding.community_and_virality: 5,000+ Slack members, 17.3k GitHub stars and 170+ contributors per its about page; swag tiers for contributors.

brand_strength.rationale: Active open source community and swag program; developer recognition but no wide consumer reach.

outcome_analysis: QuestDB grew from an open source side project into a company with a $2.3M seed in 2020 and a $12M Series A in 2021, and later released version 9.0 in July 2025 with B3 and bank customers. No later round, layoff or acquisition was found; funding is reported at about $14.3M total by TechCrunch, and the open source community is its main distribution channel.
notes: Total funding reported inconsistently ($14.3M TechCrunch, $15.3M or $18M elsewhere); TechCrunch figure used and equals recorded rounds. Seed investor list from Seedcamp congratulations and TechCrunch headline. RedMonk page was seen via search snippet only. YC page shows Ilyushchenko dates 1997 to 2019 that look inconsistent.
